summary_for_children: Adh-Dhariyat means The Scattering Winds. It swears by winds, clouds and ships, tells of Ibrahim's guests, and reminds us everything is created in pairs.
environment_concept: Winds scattering dust (51:1), clouds heavy with water (51:2), ships sailing easily (51:3) and a wide sky (51:47).
architecture_and_scenery: Dust-swept plains, heavy rain clouds, a smooth sea, and an expanding starry sky.

areas.name: Expanding Heaven
areas.description: A sky that seems to widen.

activities.name: Pairs
activities.description: Bring the animals to their pens in pairs.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Winds That Carry
story_library.children_narration: Winds can carry dust, clouds, and seeds. Surah Adh-Dhariyat begins with powerful images of movement in creation. It also tells us about the guests who came to Ibrahim and recalls the stories of Musa and other earlier peoples.

world_idea.title: The Windborne Journey
world_idea.description: Use the wind to guide lightweight objects through a landscape, explore a welcoming historical courtyard, and discover narrated story locations.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
